rationale: Evidence: iteration 5 (sensors at x = -0.05 to 0.05, y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, kp 1.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.2, last_direction) is the best raced design at 417.25. Its oval finished 20 of 20, and forward sensors (y 0.05 to 0.07) doubled s-bend progress (0.28 to 0.56). Iteration 6 tested sensor_size 0.016 at the same positions and scored lower (350.07). Oval finish fell to 0.9, s-bend progress fell to 0.29, and slalom progress fell to 0.12. The larger footprint therefore hurt, and the approved input's footprint change is already refuted by race data, so I am not repeating it. Controller gains have shown no clear lever on the tight tracks beyond kd, which is fixed at 0.4 for the oval. Slalom still shows exactly 1 line-loss event per run at a fixed point (iterations 3 to 6), with progress stuck near 0.19, so the loss is a recovery-behaviour problem rather than a geometry limit. Change: revert sensor_size to 0.012 (iteration 5 geometry) and change controller.line_loss from last_direction to search_right (signal fixed at +1, steering the robot LEFT on loss). Every other field stays at iteration 5 values, so the effect of the recovery mode is isolated. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events stay at or near 1 but the robot recovers and progress rises above 0.2, and oval and s-bend results match iteration 5. Hypotheses: (a) the slalom loss is a first-bend overshoot where a fixed search direction recovers the line better than last_direction; (b) if slalom progress drops or is unchanged with search_right, the drift is to the right and search_left is the next test. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, finish rate, line_loss_events, and the side the robot leaves the line on each track.
